implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design outputs and dissemination
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products and services to be produced, including the related systems, tools and procedures used in the Disseminate phase. Processes governing access to any confidential outputs are also designed here. Outputs should be designed to follow existing standards wherever possible, so inputs to this process may include metadata from similar or previous collections (including extractions from statistical, administrative, geospatial and other non-statistical registers and databases), international standards, and information about practices in other statistical organisations from sub-process 1.1 (Identify needs). Outputs may also be designed in partnership with other interested bodies, particularly if they are considered to be joint outputs, or they will be disseminated by another organisation.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products, and services to be produced, including all systems, tools, and procedures to be used in dissemination. Automated and AI-supported solutions are used wherever possible to produce initial output templates, align with existing standards, generate metadata, and configure dissemination tools, allowing staff to focus on innovative features and context-specific requirements, including confidentiality. All outputs and dissemination artifacts must be standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable, with support for APIs, comprehensive metadata tagging, and open formats to maximize interoperability, discoverability, and reusability by human and machine clients. The process includes an explicit, early review of the type and necessity of products, especially visualizations, with the expectation that only those genuinely required for user value or compliance are designed—allowing exclusion where end-users can self-serve or alternatives suffice. Outputs may also be designed in partnership with external organizations, ensuring full alignment with digital-to-digital workflows and standards.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' is implicated because they 'edit, validate, market, and disseminate data,' 'review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and 'interpret client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.' As output and dissemination design is automated and standardized, this officer will focus on QA, metadata validation, and supporting fit-for-purpose output design—including selection/omission of visualization types—ensuring robust machine-actionability and user-centered dissemination.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new components or reuse existing components needed for the dissemination of statistical products as designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination). All types of dissemination components are included, from those that produce traditional paper publications to those that provide web services, (linked) open data outputs, geospatial statistics, maps, or access to microdata.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new or reuse existing automation-ready dissemination components needed for the release of statistical products as designated in sub-process 2.1. Dissemination modules—spanning web services, open data, geospatial outputs, microdata access, and even traditional products—are built or upgraded for modularity, machine-actionability, and AI/automation-enabled production. Dynamic output generation, versioning, metadata enrichment, and seamless integration with downstream APIs are all standard, with automation ensuring real-time release, update, and consistency of all published outputs. Human staff are responsible for policy oversight, exception handling, and refinement of complex or user-specific dissemination features that automation cannot yet address.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update implies dissemination modules must be 'modular, API-enabled, and designed to support automated production and update of data tables, microsites, APIs, and open data endpoints.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' role includes 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'reviews and assesses data quality,' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams.' Their job is now more focused on automation-based, QA-centric, and technical oversight of dissemination component builds and upgrades, ensuring standards, interoperability, automation compatibility, and effectiveness of delivery channels.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Prepare draft outputs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process is where the data from sub-processes 5.7 (Calculate aggregates) and 5.8 (Finalise data files) are transformed into statistical outputs, which could include indexes, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, microdata, etc. The preparation of maps, GIS outputs and geo-statistical services can be included to maximise the value and capacity to analyse the statistical information. Methodological notes, to accompany the outputs and describe how they have been produced are also prepared in this sub-process taking as input the methodology designed in the Design phase. When new processing or analysis methods such as those based on machine learning or artificial intelligence are used, additional explanations might need to be prepared to communicate/explain the necessary information to the users.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process transforms processed and finalized data into statistical outputs using automated, AI-powered pipelines. Outputs—including indices, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, geo-statistical services, write-ups, dashboards, and methodological documentation—are generated by default through LLM/AI-driven automation. Human analysts intervene to interpret, refine, or tailor outputs for specialized, complex, or critical communication needs. AI-generated methodological notes and narratives accompany all outputs, documenting analytic approaches and logic. This automation-first approach maximizes efficiency, consistency, and allows analysts to focus on providing added value and insight.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used') will increasingly focus on editing and validating automatically-produced analytical and narrative products, ensuring that AI-generated content is accessible, accurate, and suitable for intended audiences.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Validate outputs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process is where statisticians validate the outputs produced, in accordance with a general quality framework and with expectations and also comparing with auxiliary information available (e.g. from previous cycles or from other sources). This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process is where outputs are validated using automated, AI- and ML-powered, real-time digital workflows. Anomaly detection, benchmarking against historical data, metadata and paradata checks, macro editing, and internal/external confrontations are executed with machine-driven QA and pattern recognition. Complex, novel, or ambiguous findings are escalated to human statistics experts for review and contextual analysis, ensuring that outputs are validated rapidly, consistently, and with high assurance of quality.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer', who 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' will be responsible for interpreting and confirming automated QA outcomes, updating validation protocols, and supporting the refinement of machine-driven validation pipelines.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Apply disclosure control
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures that the data (and metadata) to be disseminated or internally stored for future use do not breach the appropriate rules on confidentiality according to either organisational policies and rules, or to the process-specific methodology created in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). This may include checks for primary and secondary disclosure, as well as the application of data suppression or perturbation techniques and output checking. The degree and method of statistical disclosure control may vary for different types of outputs. For example, the approach used for microdata sets for research purposes will be different to that for published tables or visualisations at the aggregated level. Geospatial data or outputs from geospatial data may raise additional confidentiality challenges in terms of personal data protection and disclosure risk.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process applies disclosure control by default using AI-driven, automation-enabled privacy/SCD tools, which automatically assess, suppress, or perturb outputs for confidentiality per established policy. All actions are digitally logged and audited. Outputs only reach human reviewers when the automation detects elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks, ensuring privacy compliance by default and at scale.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Disclosure control is now performed by 'AI-driven, automation-enabled privacy/SCD tools,' with staff reviewing 'elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer', who is involved in 'editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data' and is 'responsible for the application of data suppression or perturbation techniques and output checking,' will become the principal authority in reviewing flagged disclosure risks, confirming privacy decisions escalated by AI, and documenting disclosure rationale and actions.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Finalise outputs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures the statistics and associated information are fit for purpose and reach the required quality level and are thus ready for use. It includes: Completing consistency checks; Determining the level of release, and applying caveats; Collating supporting information, including interpretation, commentary, technical notes, briefings, measures of uncertainty and any other necessary metadata; Producing the supporting internal documents; Conducting pre-release discussion with appropriate internal subject matter experts; Translating the statistical outputs in countries with multilingual dissemination; Approving the statistical content for release.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process finalises and packages outputs using digital, automation-driven tools and workflows, ensuring all required metadata, commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and documentation are produced and collated automatically to the highest standard. Human experts are responsible for sign-off, review of flagged anomalies, and decision-making on exceptional release scenarios or nuanced dissemination requirements. Routine approval, translation, and pre-release briefing are streamlined by digital platforms, maximizing output quality and deployment speed.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM requires 'automation for all routine checks, collation, evidence-gathering, and documentation for dissemination,' reserving human involvement for quality assurance and complex scenarios. The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer,' with expertise in 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' and 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output… analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' will verify automated output packages, complete QA review, approve for release, and handle nuanced or exceptional dissemination scenarios.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Disseminate
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase manages the release of the statistical data and their products to users. It includes all activities associated with assembling and releasing a range of static and dynamic products via a range of channels. These activities support users to access and use the products released by the statistical organisation. For statistical products produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. Cataloguing and tagging released data and products using relevant metadata standards can greatly increase their discoverability and accessibility both internally and externally. International standards should be used as a norm to ensure that they can be found and consumed easily across a broad range of users. Linking data to geospatial classifications in particular can allow for detailed geographical presentation of outputs. While GSBPM conceives of archiving as taking place within the overarching Data Management and Metadata Management activities, its relevance to finalised outputs in this phase should be noted. The Disseminate phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase manages the release of statistical data and their products to users using automation-driven, API-first, and metadata-enriched delivery workflows and platforms. All assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, and release processes are automated and performed in real-time, producing products that are dynamically accessible, searchable, and machine-actionable by both human and AI agents. Outputs are prepared for API-driven consumption, optimized for AI search, and enriched with comprehensive metadata to ensure discovery and reuse across systems. Human staff engage only for policy setting, exception handling, and specialized user support. The Disseminate phase is structured into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which may operate sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as best fits the digital dissemination ecosystem.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM now mandates full automation and digitization for dissemination—'all assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, and release processes are automated and performed in real-time, producing products that are dynamically accessible, searchable, and machine-actionable.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer', who 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams', is now focused on overseeing these automated data release platforms, advising on metadata enrichment, troubleshooting exceptions, and supporting users in digital-first dissemination environments.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Update output systems
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes, including: Formatting data and metadata ready to be put into output systems; Loading data and metadata into output systems; Ensuring data are linked to the relevant metadata. Formatting, loading and linking of metadata should preferably mostly take place in earlier phases, but this sub-process includes a final check that all of the necessary metadata are in place ready for dissemination.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process manages the update of output systems and databases for dissemination using automated, real-time loading of data and enriched metadata. Machine-actionable formatting, digital linkage, and metadata validation are built-in, ensuring that all disseminated products are AI- and API-consumable, searchable, and enriched with discoverability standards. Final checks for completeness and metadata enrichment are automatic, and all outputs are designed for seamless use by both human and digital consumers.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update requires output systems to be 'auto-loading, metadata-enriched, machine-actionable outputs, ready for API-driven digital release.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('provides statistical data and consultative services to users', 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata') will supervise the metadata enrichment, ensure linkages are complete for discoverability, and validate the technical correctness of machine-actionable outputs before release.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Produce dissemination products
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process produces the dissemination products, as previously designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination), to meet user needs. They could include publications, press releases and websites. The products can take many forms including interactive graphics, tables, maps, public-use microdata sets, linked open data and downloadable files. When the final products raise concern for confidentiality, additional disclosure control may be considered and applied via sub-process 6.4 (Apply disclosure control). Typical steps include: Preparing the product components (explanatory texts, tables, charts, maps, quality statements etc.); Assembling the components into products; Editing the products and checking that they meet publication standards.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process produces dissemination outputs using automated, AI- and LLM-powered workflows to generate, assemble, and format all products—including publications, press releases, online tables, interactive graphics, maps, and PUMFs—as standard. Text, graphics, and narrative products are created with digital automation as first resort, and all products (including mandatory PUMFs) are checked for standards adherence by human specialists, who refine outputs and ensure audience appropriateness as required. All dissemination outputs are machine-actionable, metadata-enriched, and ready for instant digital release.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Production must be 'automated and AI-driven,' with LLMs drafting all textual and visualization products for human review and refinement. The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('edits, validates... disseminates data', 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output') becomes a key reviewer, validator, and adapter of AI-created reports, tables, summaries, graphics, and—when required—Public Use Microdata Files (PUMFs).

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Release dissemination products
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures that all elements for the release are in place including managing the timing of the release. It includes briefings for specific groups such as the press or ministers, as well as the arrangements for any pre-release embargoes. It also includes the provision of products to subscribers, and managing access to confidential data by authorised user groups, such as researchers. Sometimes an organisation may need to retract a product, for example, if an error is discovered. This is also included in this sub-process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process releases dissemination products using digital automation to handle all elements of release—timing, briefing, embargo, subscriber access, and confidential data management. Orchestration platforms schedule, log, and manage real-time releases. Human staff review and approve exception cases, interact with high-level subscribers, and handle policy or retraction scenarios as required, ensuring transparency and compliance at all times.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Release, timing, access and embargo management are handled via 'orchestrated, automated, and logged digital systems.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('participates on data production and dissemination teams,' 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users') will focus on exception review, approval of high-profile or embargoed releases, and liaison with key clients such as researchers.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Promote dissemination products
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: Whilst marketing in general can be considered to be part of GAMSO, this sub-process concerns the active promotion of the statistical products produced in a specific statistical business process, to help them reach the widest possible audience. It includes the use of customer relationship management tools, to better target potential users of the products, as well as the use of tools including websites and other platforms like social media to facilitate the process of communicating statistical information to users. These activities may be coordinated with partners in the case of joint products.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process promotes statistical products using AI/automation-driven tools to generate, recommend, and deploy messaging across all platforms—web, email, social, and beyond. Content, format, and strategy are tailored with AI for each target audience, adjusting to maximize reach and impact. Staff intervene for high-level campaign review, optimization, and the management of complex or sensitive outreach.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Promotion is now 'automated and AI-driven, with messaging, format, and channel recommendations adjusted in real time.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' (whose duties include 'markets and disseminates data,' and 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data') must review, validate, and optimize AI-prompted outreach messages and campaigns, and is responsible for quality assurance of critical communications across platforms.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Provide user support
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures that user queries and requests for services such as microdata access are recorded, and that responses are provided within agreed deadlines. These queries and requests should be regularly reviewed to provide an input to the overarching Quality Management activity, as they can indicate new or changing user needs. Replies to user requests can also be used to populate a knowledge database or a “Frequently Asked Questions” page, that is made publicly available, thus reducing the burden of replying to repeated and/or similar requests from external users. This sub-process also includes managing support to any partner organisations involved in disseminating the products.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process provides user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces, which record, triage, and answer user queries in real time, guiding users to datasets, data interpretations, and publications as needed. Complex inquiries and escalations go to human staff for resolution, especially for nuanced, sensitive, or high-value support. User feedback and request tracking are used to populate knowledge bases and feed into service quality improvement.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM requires 'user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' (responsible for 'providing statistical data and consultative services to users') will be escalated complex or high-priority queries, oversee knowledgebase curation, and provide input on improving AI/automated FAQ and support workflows.
